Jbel Toubkal, located about 60 kilometers south of Marrakesh in Morrocco, is the highest point of, FTP, what mountain range of Northwestern Africa?

The third-largest city and only major seaport of the state of this name is Salina Cruz, while other major cities include Huajuapan de Leon and Juchitan de Zaragoza. The state is known as the land of the Seven Moles (pron.: Moh-leh), while the city of this name sits at the site of the old Aztec fort of Huaxyaca in the junction of a Y-shaped valley of the same name. San Juan Bautista Tuxtepec is the second-largest city in the state, which borders Puebla and Gurrero to west, Veracruz to the north and Chiapas to the east. The center of the Zapotec civilization and the hometown of Benito Juarez, FTP identify this large southern Mexican state located in the Sierra Madre and its capital of the same name.

Its minor tributaries include the Sacandaga, the Hoosic and the Schroon, while towns along its banks include Stillwater, Glens Falls, Kingston and Ossining. Known in Mahican as Muh-he-kun-ne-tuk, or "the river that goes two ways," it is a tidal estuary as far upstream as Troy. Parts of this river form coves such as Haverstraw Bay and Weehawken Cove, the former of which is just north of this river's widest part, the Tappan Zee. It is connected to the Delaware by a namesake canal, and its principal tributary is the Mohawk. FTP, name this river that flows past Jersey City, Albany and Manhattan.

The little river of this name is diverted into the reservoir at Fort Loudon by the Tellico dam. The larger one is joined by the Clinch River shortly after its formation from the junction of the Holston and French Broad rivers. It gave its name to the army commanded by Oliver Howard and James B. McPherson, while its later history featured dam construction at Pickwick Landing, Guntersville, and Watts Bar. FTP, name this American river redeveloped by a New Deal agency.

This city's Trianon Park lies close to a structure utilizing right-angled solidium beams in a litter to carry MASP [rhymes with "hasp," not "wasp"]. This city's Week of Modern Art featured paintings by Anita Malfatti and Emiliano di Cavalcanti, a reading from Hallucinated City by Mário Andrade, and performances of works by Heitor Villa-Lobos. Its BOVESPA ["boh-VES-puh"] stock exchange is the largest in Latin America. A riverbank in this city was the site of the Grito de Ipiranga, the proclamation by Dom Pedro I of Brazilian independence. FTP name this most populous city in the Southern Hemisphere.

In the south of this country, the Rupununi Savanna provides hunting grounds for the Wapisiana and Macusi tribes, and the Kunuku Range hinders access to its gold and diamond mining center. The sources of rivers like the Mazaruni and Cununi are found in its western Pakaraima Range near its highest point, Mt. Roraima. Marshall Falls blocks southward progress along its most important river at its second largest city, Bartica. That river, the Essequibo, meets the Atlantic west of its capital, the largest English speaking city in South America. FTP, name this country with capital Georgetown.

The western half of the region in which they are found comprised the Phelps and Gorham Purchase of 1790, the world's largest land purchase at the time. Their southern ends are characterized by glacial hanging valleys leading to waterfalls in such areas as Fillmore Glen and Watkins Glen. There are eleven of them in total and four of them – Conesus, Hemlock, Canadice, and Otisco – are known as the "minor" ones. Several of them are named for Indian tribes once indigenous to the area, including Owasco, Cayuga, and Senega. FTP, name this group of thin lakes in upstate New York.

Among the main tributaries always leading off to the right of this river are the Cher and Indre Rivers, both of which come off before the series of large dikes that protect its lower course. It is canalized for many miles of its passage and is connected by canals to the Saone River and the harbor of Brest. It rises in the Cevennes Mountains and flows 634 miles before flowing through a 35-mile estuary into the Bay of Biscay. FTP, name this longest river of France.

It rises in the Kailas Range and is known by several names along its course until the city of Sadiya at which point it changes names from the Dihang to its best-known name. In ancient times it was known by one of two other names, Dyardanes or Oedanes. It flows south for another 500 miles before dividing into two channels, one of which is the Jamuna River. By that time it has already run a 900-mile eastward course through Tibet. FTP, name this 1,800 mile long river that joins the Ganges Delta before flowing into the Bay of Bengal.

Sunfish Pond lies directly south of this geographical entity, which passes north-south through Wayah Bald. The towns of Pearisburg and Duncannon lie along this route, whose Abol Bridge marks the end of its passage through the Hundred-Mile Wilderness. From the Lakes of the Clouds, it parallels the oldest mountain cog railway, up Mount Washington. It descends to Newfound Gap from Clingmans Dome, this route's high point. At its lowest point, Bear Mountain Bridge, it crosses the ► Hudson, while the headquarters of its "Conservancy" are at Harpers Ferry. White blazes from Springer Mountain, Georgia, to Mount Katahdin, Maine mark, what 2,000 mile trail, popular among "thru-hikers," along a namesake East Coast mountain range?

The Blaan and Tboli are this island's native peoples. Tubod lies across Panguil Bay from Ozamiz in this island's Misamis Occidental province. Maria Cristina Falls is located on the Agus River in its city of Iligan, and this island's ports include Cotabato, General Santos City, and Cagayan de Oro. East of its Zamboanga Peninsula lies Lake Lanao, and Mount Apo is its highest volcano. This island lies south of the Bohol Sea, which separates it from the Visayas, and the Surigao Strait separates it from Leyte. A revolt has occurred among Muslim ► Moro people on this island, whose largest city is Davao. Name this island in the southern Philippines, second in land area to Luzon.

Erchite Wood and Torr Wood lie along this body of water. Boleskine House was constructed next to this body of water, which is fed by the Fall of Foyers, and Bona Narrows lies along it. The town of Dores sits on its shore, while Whitebridge is a few miles from its banks. The sole island in this body of water is Cherry Island. The villages of Invermoriston and Drumnadrochit, along with Urquhart Castle, overlook this lake. Dr. Robert Wilson's photograph of this lake neglected to show a submerged submarine. At the southern end of this lake in the Great Glen Fault, it meets the River Oich at Fort Augustus, and it is connected by the ► Caledonian Canal to Inverness. Name this long lake in the highlands of Scotland, home to an apocryphal "monster."

The town of El Búfalo lies in this state, along with Satevó and Urique. The Recohuata Hot Springs are located in this state, along with Lake Arareco and the Samalayuca Dunes. Near Janos in this state, archeological digs occur at Paquimé. This state's town of Creel, a stop on the "El Chepe" train, lies roughly 50 miles from Basaseachic Falls. At Ojinaga in this state, the Río Conchos ends, and it is home to the cities of Delicias and Parral. Deeper in parts than Arizona's Grand Canyon, Copper Canyon lies in its southwest. Its capital shares its name, while its largest city, across the ► Rio Grande from El Paso, is Ciudad Juárez. Name this state bordering New Mexico, Sonora, and Texas, the largest in Mexico, which lends its name to a breed of small dogs.
Free and Sovereign State of Chihuahua

This nation's city of Kryvyi Rih is a center of its steel industry. Three oblasts in this country's eastern end form a coal-mining region called the Donbass, the basin of the Donets River. One politician from this country was the subject of an assassination attempt using TCDD, a powerful dioxin; that man overcame electoral fraud to lead the ► Orange Revolution. This nation's city of Uman and its capital were the scenes of encirclement battles during Operation Barbarossa, which resulted in the massacre of 34,000 Jews at a ravine outside a city on the Dnieper River. The Babi Yar massacre took place in what former Soviet republic, whose cities include Lviv, Odessa, and Kiev?

The highest point on this island is Mount Desor, which rises 240 meters above the surrounding waters. The Treaty of La Pointe in 1842 caused this island to be in two countries simultaneously, until an eponymously named treaty in 1844 settled the dispute. In 1897, its eponymously named country was dissolved, and the island was incorporated into Keweenaw County, about 55 miles to its southeast. In 1940, this island became part of an eponymously named national park, and National Park ferries connect this island to Grand Portage, Minnesota, as well as Houghton and Copper Harbor. This island was the site of a study examining cyclic fluctuations in the ► populations of wolves and moose. Name this Michigan island in Lake Superior.

In 1994, Ruth Shady Solis began excavating in this country's Norte Chico region, at a site known as Caral, which was dated to be founded before 2600 BCE. Further north, along the Fortaleza River, is the even older site of Huaricanga, which is dated to 3500 BCE. In the southern part of this country, in the Osmore River Valley, is Cerro Baul, a large mesa which was the meeting point for two ancient cultures who both worshiped the "Staff God," the Wari and the Tiwanaku. Also in this country was the Chimor culture, whose capital was at Chan Chan. ► name this country which is better known for sites of the Inkan civilization such as Machu Picchu and Nazca.

Though it is not Spain, this place is home to mountains named Valterne, Tortelosa, and Gayne. While it was forming, aluminum-26 and iron-60 provided a large amount of heat, making its interior warm and squishy, causing it to spin rapidly. This moon is home to an equatorial ridge of mountains that go nearly around the moon, and its craters, including Clarin, Almeric, Bramimond, and Charlemagne, as well as its Roncevaux Terra, derive their names from the Song of Roland. For 15 points, identify this walnut-shaped and distinctly two- toned moon discovered by Cassini, the ► third largest surrounding Saturn.

Th-century farmlands surrounding this entity were known as "the Smeeth." The world's first parabolic reflector shone across this body of water from the Hunstanton Lighthouse. The Great Ouse, Steeping, and Witham rivers flow into this body of water, and there are more seals here than anywhere else in the UK. Its hinterlands include the cities of Holme Next the Sea, King's Lynn, and Boston. This body of water collects water from 10% of England's land, and it is located where Lincolnshire meets Norfolk. Opening into the North Sea, this is, for 15 points, what square-mouthed estuary, the largest in the UK?

This mountain's namesake built a defensive fortification at West Point and suggested that an academy be built there, and that name was given to this mountain by Paul Edmund Strzelecki. Rawson's pass is located just below this mountain's summit, and is home to a famous toilet. Names for this mountain in a native language all mean "Table Top Mountain" and include Targangil and Jagungal. Some climbers believe that instead of this mountain, the Carstensz Pyramid in Irian Jaya should be considered one of the ► Seven Summits. Located in the Snowy Mountains, this is, what mountain in the Great Dividing Range, the tallest on mainland Australia?

One region of this country is home to the districts of Herale and Ceelbuur. That region, Galguduud, has a capital which was the site of March 20, 2012 fighting with Ahlusunna Waljamaa, and which was previously held by Ahlu-Sunnah wal-Jamah, the city of Dhusamareb. This country's highest peak is a part of the Cal Madow range, mount Shimbiri. Coastal cities include Xiis, which is near Raas Surud, and ► Kismaayo. This country is home to the Oromo region and the regional state of Puntland. Identify this country on the horn of Africa, separated from Arabia by the Gulf of Aden, with capital at Mogadishu.

One suburb of this city is home to the Cream Gables Bed and Breakfast, and that suburb is New Farm. A mostly underground mountain has its summit in this city, Mount Coot-Tha. This city is also home to Whites Hill and Enoggera Hill. This city is home to the stadium of Lang Park, and it is also the location of Gifford University. Cyclone Whitney caused a 1974 flood here, which flooded this city's botanical gardens and relocated some Mangroves. Free settlement did not begin here until 1842, though tt was founded as a ► Penal Colony in 1824 by John Oxley. Located in land first claimed by James Cook on the East Coast of Australia, this is, what third most populous city of Australia and capital of Queensland?

One island on this body of water is home to three villages – Tooni, Saare, and Piiri. The last of those villages is home to a church of Old Believers, founded by the first inhabitants of that island of Piirissaar. Towns on the banks of this body of water include Gdov and Mustvee, and one city on its banks is home to the Mirozhsky Monastery, Pskov. The Velikaya River flows into this lake, and it is drained by the Narva. One part of this lake is called ► Lämmijärv, and another is known as Pihkva. The largest trans- boundary lake in Europe is, what lake on the border of Estonia and Russia, the site of the 1242 Battle of the Ice?

Houston has two of these entities, one of which is named for Sam Houston, while one of these in Las Vegas is named for Bruce Woodbury. These entities have aided development and growth in cities such as Dunwoody, Georgia and Carmel, Indiana. Foreign ones include the M25 and Beijing has five of these, while the longest in the United States is Interstate 275, which is between five and fifteen miles from downtown Cincinnati. These roads name the baseball series between the Orioles and the ► Nationals. The most famous one passes Tysons Corner, Virginia and metonymically separates government insiders from the rest of America. Name this type of highway, such as Interstate 495 going around Washington, DC.

The Nilgiri Hills are in the western part of this state near its second- largest city of Coimbatore, and the Pallavi Kingdom was centered in this present-day state at Kanchipuram, one of the holiest cities in Hinduism. This state is home to the delta of the Kaveri River, which flows into the state from Karnataka. This state, which borders on the Gulf of Mannar and has the northern terminus of Adam's Bridge, surrounds the city of Pondicherry. Lying east of Kerala and south of Andhra Pradesh, this state was formerly known as Madras State, and members of this state's namesake ethnic group tried to create a breakaway republic in nearby Sri Lanka. For 15 points, name this state of southern India with capital at Chennai.

Prehistoric civilizations on this island erected large stone slabs called giant's graves, which contain burial chambers. Also prehistoric and on this island are a bunch of tower-like forts called nuraghi. The language of Algherese, a variant of Catalan, is spoken only in the northwestern portion of this island. The Tirso River is the longest on this island, and its only natural freshwater lake is Lago di Baratz. This island's capital is Cagliari. This island is bordered to the east by the ► Tyrrhenian Sea, and the Strait of Bonifacio separates it from Corsica. Name this large Mediterranean island owned by Italy that was ruled by Victor Emmanuel II along with the Piedmont before Italian unification.

This country's northeast contains the Mafinag Hills. This country's second largest city contains a landmark that in the 2000s fell due to unknown circumstances, the Slave Tree. The limestone industry is the most important to that city, Ndola. The world's largest artificial lake, Lake Kariba, lies on this country's southern borders. This country contains the southern portion of the Copperbelt and was called ►Northern Rhodesia before becoming independent. The Congo Pedicle juts into this country, which was an issue that led to several conflicts. This country borders Lake Tanganyika to the east and Angola to the west. Name this African country which shares Victoria Falls with Zimbabwe and has its capital at Lusaka.

Locations in this body of water included an island that contained dwarfish species, leading Franz Nopcsa to coin what would become Foster's rule. That location in this body of water contained Telmatosaurs and Magyarosaurs and was called Hateg Island. This body of water formed after the Cimmerian plate moved northward, which put it in the same location as a similarly-named predecessor. The formation of the Indian Ocean caused this body of water to shrink, and its remnants include the ► Mediterranean and Arabian Seas. Name this ancient body of water which formed from the breakup of Pangaea during the Triassic, a sea separating Laurasia from Gondwana and named after the wife of Oceanus.

The 12th hole of this island's Jack Nicklaus-designed golf course, The Challenge at Manele, was the site of Bill and Melinda Gates' wedding. Traditionally, for administrative purposes this island was divided into 13 Ahupuaʻa, though the firm Castle and Cooke and later the private businessman David Murdock became significant landowners. The 'Au'Au Channel separates it from its eastern neighbor while the Kalohi Channel separates it from its Northern neighbor, and it is part of a county named for an island to its east as well. ► name this sixth largest of the Hawaiian islands, once home to the world's largest pineapple plantation which lies to the south of Molokai and the east of Maui.

This island group was where Grant Hadwin disappeared after chopping down the Kiidk'yaas, a rare golden mutation of the Sitka spruce in the Yakoun valley. Dawson's subspecies of caribou once lived on Graham Island in this group, whose "spirit" appears in the carving of a jade canoe by Bill Reid. The Dixon Entrance, which separates these islands from southern Alaska, is named after sailor George Dixon, who gave them their English name honoring the ► consort of George III. The Haida people live on what island group off the coast of British Columbia?

This country's northwestern neighbor is home to the Gonarezhou National park, which lies along its border with this country, and the Ruyuma rivers forms the border between this country and its northern neighbor. The Monte Binga is the highest mountain in this country, and the Inhambane bay forms an inlet into this country. The southern town of Ponta d'Ouro is a popular tourist destination in this country. The Bazaruto archipelago lies off the coast of this African country, whose city of Beira is its second largest, and the Limpopo and Zambezi rivers empty into a waterway named for this country. Bordered by South Africa, Zambia, Malawi, Zimbabwe, and Lesotho, and having its capital at Maputo, identify this country separated from Madagascar by a namesake channel.

One of the names of this country's largest lakes literally translates as "Booze Vat" and is a stunning green color. Its Central Highlands region is home to the "Hals" topography and such cities as Borgarnes. Its only native tree is the Betula pubsescens birch, which is being deforested because of topsoil erosion. This country's north is home to Dettifoss, the largest waterfall by volume in Europe, and Akureryi is the country's largest city outside the capital metropolitan area. This country's island of Surtsey emerged from the ocean in the 1960s. Vatnajökull covers 8% of the country, and has been the scene of Jökulhlaup, spectacular glacial eruptions and floods. Name this North Atlantic island nation, home to Björk and unpronounceable place names.

The economy of this state's rural northwest region boomed in 1950 when uranium was discovered at Grants. As early as 1922, this state had a female secretary of state, Soledad Chacon. A noted shootout in this state occurred after its denizen Oliver M. Lee was implicated in the disappearance of Albert Jennings Fountain. The Civil War campaign in this state culminated when an undermanned Confederate force under Henry Hopkins Sibley defeated E.R.S Canby at Valverde. One of its native peoples was forced to undergo the "Long Walk to Bosque Redondo" after the Treaty of Fort Sumner was signed in this state. This state was the home of the lavish mansion of the Secretary of the Interior during the Teapot Dome scandal, who was previously a senator from this state. Name this home state of Albert Fall, whose capital is the oldest in the U.S., and is called Santa Fe.

The Delft Island is located off of this country, and Mundal Lake lies along its west coast. One can observe estuarine crocodiles from the Kirindi Oya river in the Bundala National Park located in this country. The Kalu River is the second longest river in this country and to its west lies the Gulf of Mannar. The Knuckles mountain range is located in this country, and the city of Jaffna is located in its north. The Esala Perahara is an important festival in a city which houses the Asigiriya Cricket stadium, and visitors there should not miss the temple containing the sacred tooth of the Buddha. In addition to Kandy, this country's gem shopping center is located at Ratnapura, and one can see several ancient Buddhist sites in the city of Anuradhaputra. Somehow connected to its northern neighbor via Adam's Bridge, identify this country whose largest city is Colombo.
Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

Among this nation's offshore possessions are the Serrana Bank and San Andrés island. The San Bernardo archipelago is found off the coast of this country, whose northernmost most point on its mainland is Point Gallinas, located on the Guajira Peninsula. Much of its southern border is formed by the Putamayo River, while the Guaviare and Meta are other major rivers in this country and its highest point is Pico Cristóbal. Major cities such as Manizales and Bucaramanga lie in the densely-populated mountain valleys that are drained by the northward-flowing Magdalena River, which enters the Caribbean at Barranquila. Identify this home of Medellin and Cali, a South American nation with capital at Bogota.

Its highest point is the Adelungha Toghi at above 14,000 feet, and its lowest point, in lake Sarikamish, is below sea level. Dominated in the north by the Qizilqum Desert, it has a fertile area in the Fergana Valley, where the Naryn and the Kara Darya come together near Namangan to form the Syr Darya. Nukus is the capital of the autonomous republic of Karakalpakstan, which occupies its western end; other major cities include Jizzax and Bukhara. The only one of the five Central Asian states to border the other four, name, FTP, this former Soviet republic containing the cities of Samarqand and Tashkent.

This nation's Gorongosa National Park is home to seven miniature antelope species, and is located north of the city of Beira. Cabo Delgado is located south of the Rovuma River, which forms this nation's northern border. Its province of Niassa has capital at Lichinga, and borders both Lake Malawi and the country of Malawi. Its northwest province of Tete is home to Lake Cahora Bassa, which was formed after the building of a dam on the Zambezi river. This country is also home to the delta of the Zambezi River on the Indian Ocean. Name this African nation with capital at Maputo.

Cities in this geographical region include Santa Laura and Maria Helena, and a large source of revenue comes from its Calama basin. Lying mainly between the south bend of the Loa River and the mountains separating the Salado-Copiapó drainage basin, this region is under the control of a nation acquired it in the 1883 Treaty of Ancon. Salt flats stretching from the Andean foothills make up a significant portion of this region. Copper mines at Chuquicamata and mineral deposits northwest of Antofagasta containing sodium nitrate have made this area the subject of conflict in the War of the Pacific. Identify this South American desert, a cool region that defines a border with Peru but is primarily found in Northern Chile.

In the Mountain of the Sky is a bird with six feet, four legs, no face and a body entirely of this color. In the land of Kunlun, a tree on top of a palace of pure jade has leaves of this color jade, because this color jade was held to be the rarest. This was also the color of the bow owned by Youhi, who used it to shoot down nine of the ten suns. It was also held to be the color of the Chinese phoenix, because it is traditionally held to be the color of luck. Name this color of the gold-embossed envelopes containing huge wads of cash during Chinese New Year, which also titles a novel about Jin Baoyu, who has a dream in this type of chamber.

For his role in slaying the large centipede that dwelt nearby Lake Biwa, the hero Hidesato was given a roll of silk, a pair of bells and a pouch containing this. Chinese legend states that the Buddha was appeased when he was offered four containers of this substance by the kings of the four directions. A god whose domain was this substance transformed into a spider to torment the wicked and was bisexual. When that god of this domain died, cattle, silkworms and plants sprung from his body. Identify this delicious stuff that was the domain of Inari, which can be used to make the alcoholic beverage sake.

One woman born in this country drinks from the river of hate while a knight from Italy drinks from the river of love. Warlocks from this country are able to summon demons, which a brother-sister pair do in order to chain a magician under the ocean. During a siege of this country's capital, its king recognizes the horse Rabican that he gave to his son. A prince and princess from this country are guarded over by four giants that are put to sleep by Malagigi. This country is ruled over by King Galafron out of its capital of Albraca. It is the birthplace of the knight Argalia, who brings his sister Angelica along to demoralize Charlemagne's knights. Name this country central to Orlando Inamorato, the archaic name for China and sometimes India.

The Bogda Mountains is an eastern extension of this mountain range, and this mountain range is the source of the Chu River. Tianchi is an alpine lake in this mountain range, which runs north of the Turpan Depression. The South Ingylchek Glacier is the largest area of ice in this mountain range and lies under Khan Tengri, which along with Pik Pobedy is one of the highest peaks in this range. The Naryn River rises in this mountain range and is the main feeder of the Syr Darya. This mountain range runs near Urumqi and the Taklamakan Desert and it contains the large Lake Issyk-Kul as well as the city of Bishkek.FTP, name this mountain range that runs through Xinjiang Province in China and through Kyrgyzstan, which has a name that means heavenly mountains.

The terrible climate of this country's Savannakhet region helped stifle nefarious coup-inciting by the "Programs Evaluation Office." This country's namesake language, which is spoken with an extra tone in a city whose Xieng Thong Temple survived its near-annihilation during the Haw Wars, underwent a series tonal conversion as it migrated down the Nam Ou river during the fifteenth century. That language underwent a major simplification reform in the 1960s, which helped distinguish it from another country's Isan dialect, spoken heavily across its Southwestern border. This state's origins lie in Fa Ngum's expansion into Sainyabuli, for which he supposedly received an open- palmed gold statue, the Phra Bang, from a Lovek king. The Lan Xang Empire built this country's "Army of The Million Elephants," and its city of Pakxe was a target for the disastrous Lam Son 719 and Barrel Roll operations, which left land mines strewn across its Plain of Jars. This country defines the Eastern bound of the heroin-producing "Golden Triangle," and lies across the Mekong from Thailand. FTP, name this landlocked country in Southeast Asia, whose capital is Vientiane.

Speakers of the northern dialect of Gheg in this country are separated from speakers of the southern Tosk dialect by the Shkumbin River. Vlachs are one of the ethnic minorities of this predominantly Moslem country that contains the cities of Vlore and Durres, the latter of which was known to the Greeks as Epidamnus and the Venetians as Durazzo and lies across the Straits of Otranto from Brindisi. Name this country which Enver Hoxha once governed from the capital of Tirane.

The region includes Keuka Lake, which is one of its state's main wine- growing sections, as well as a "Women's Rights National Historical Park." Otisco is the easternmost and Conesus the westernmost, Watkins Glen is at the south end of Seneca and Ithaca is just south of Cayuga in, what region of central New York named for bodies of water formed by glaciers?
